newsitem.title: USA: BPA says generation even with long-term contracts.
newsitem.headline: BPA says generation even with long-term contracts.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) withdrew Thursday from offering next-day power in the spot market because its generation resources are roughly balanced with long-term sales commitments, sources at the agency said.
"We have just enough to meet our own loads and long-term contracts," a BPA trader said.
Another source at the agency said reservoir levels at the key Grand Coulee dam in Washington have reached minimum operating levels due to the recent cooler-than-normal weather in the region.
"Loads were greater than we anticipated, but this is a short-term situation. One week at the most," he predicted.
The first BPA trader also noted that the lack of surplus is not related to the reduction in power generation from Washington Public Power Supply System's 1,158 megawatt (MW) nuclear plant.

Output from the nuclear plant, all of which is marketed by Bonneville, is expected to dip to 55 or 65 percent of capacity later today while work is carried out on recirculation pump drives. The reduction was expected to last less than one day.
